subject: Transportation Systems
title: Maglev: Floating on Magnets
description: A 60-second lesson on Maglev: Floating on Magnets.

hook.text: A maglev train floats above the track. No wheels, no friction, no contact at all.

buildup.text: Superconducting magnets create a field that lifts the train and propels it forward simultaneously.

discovery.text: Japan's SCMaglev hit 374 mph in testing—the fastest any rail vehicle has ever traveled.

twist.text: Maglev track is incompatible with conventional rail. You can't share infrastructure. Costs are enormous.

climax.text: Only three commercial maglev lines exist worldwide. The technology works, but the economics rarely do.

punchline.text: Maglev solved the physics. It hasn't solved the price tag.

quiz.question: Why haven't more maglev lines been built worldwide?
options: Track is incompatible with existing rail and extremely expensive
